value.rules_markdown:
- Use `src/` as the single crate; one responsibility per module, core types in module-local `types.rs`, every port in `src/ports/` is one trait in one file.
- In `src/bin/tinysweeper.rs`, declare every CLI subcommand even if its milestone has not landed; `src/server/` is the only production surface, not distributed/run as a GitHub Action.
- Presets are review policy as data, not code: a preset is a folder with `preset.toml`, `README.md`, optional prompt overrides; adding a preset is a new folder, never a new module.
- Never edit `vendor/tinyagents` here; change it upstream and bump the git submodule pin.
- Write one document per `src/` module at `docs/modules/<module>/README.md`.
- Declare `examples/` explicitly in `Cargo.toml` with `required-features` so credential-needing smoke tests never build in CI.
- Run `git submodule update --init --recursive`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, and `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`.
- Run `cargo test --locked` and `cargo check --locked --all-features --all-targets`.
- Keep the default build offline: no HTTP client linked, test suite never touches network; put network-needing functionality behind features (`harness`, `github`, `serve`).
- Use rustfmt output and Rust 2024 idioms; `snake_case` modules/files, `PascalCase` types.
- Return `Result<T>` using the crate error type from `src/error.rs`.
- Every file opens with a `//!` module doc describing its role and any feature gating.
- Comments explain the decision, not the code; when a flag or ordering is load-bearing, say so and why.
- Public items carry doc comments; Clap fields use `///` because it becomes the help text.
- Tests live in-crate: a `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` block at the bottom of the module, moving to a sibling `test.rs` or `<name>_test.rs` when they grow; no `tests/` directory.
- Every port has an always-compiled offline mock; `MockForge` records what would have been written so tests can assert exact check runs and comments.
- Cover lane behaviour with golden tests: fixture diff plus canned structured model response, asserting findings that survive filtering, dedupe, and capping.
- Maintain at least 80% coverage for meaningful library behaviour.
- Keep every Markdown file, including repository guidelines, at 500 lines or fewer; split and link when a topic grows past that limit.
- Model never holds write token; lanes run read-only; write credentials minted only in `src/apply/` after all model calls; a lane leaving a change fails.
- Contributor code is never executed: read the diff and tree, do not build, install dependencies, or run target repository scripts.
- Treat PR bodies, comments, diffs as untrusted input; fence/label them as data in prompts; model verdict advisory; only deterministic policy in `src/apply/` and `src/automerge/` may mutate GitHub.
- Secrets found by scanners are reported by type and location only; the value never reaches a comment, a check-run summary, or a log.
- Use concise, imperative commit subjects; keep commits small and each coherent validated slice on its own; PRs state what changed, any behaviour change, and how it was verified.
